summary: Delete a project record and all of its image assets in one IndexedDB transaction so whole-project deletion is all-or-nothing.

impactAnalysis.notes: F-023 is specifically the whole-project deletion atomicity gap. The implementation will add one project-store operation that opens a single readwrite transaction spanning both the projects and image-assets object stores, deletes matching project assets and the project record inside that transaction, and updates the main deletion and failed-import cleanup paths to call that canonical operation. Existing DB/schema constants remain unchanged; F-032 storage ownership duplication is reviewed but intentionally not remediated here. No Item/BOM, placement, renderer, catalog, project schema, or import archive format semantics are intentionally changed.

e2e.reason: Project deletion is browser-visible persistence/storage behavior. Chromium must prove that deleting a project removes both its project record and its image assets while leaving another project's data intact.

risk.notes: The deletion boundary moves from two independent transactions to one cross-store transaction. Main risks are deleting assets belonging to another project, failing to delete all target assets, or changing failed-import cleanup behavior. Targeted storage/integration and browser tests cover those boundaries.

migration.notes: No IndexedDB version, object-store schema, project schema, or persisted record shape changes.

rollback: Revert the atomic project+asset deletion API, restore the previous two-step main deletion/cleanup calls, and remove the targeted regressions.
